overlap.note: the categories overlap: the candidates accepted by the checks include those outside the pool limit, and a candidate can be both excluded by requirements and failed numerically; the counts need not sum to the pool size

agent.label: Deadzone
agent.reason: Recommend `Deadzone`: its symmetric dead-zone input map is compact and balances two validation designs. Leave-one-trajectory-out free-run RMSE of `y` is `0.125475` in unspecified output units; first-100-row fitting and final-50-transition validation gives `0.103553` in the same units. `Rational` has lower trajectory-held-out RMSE (`0.111305`) but weaker prefix-tail performance (`0.137843`) and a singularity outside the nonnegative-input domain. `Smooth` fits training much better but has weaker held-out-trajectory performance. All values were computed on `data/train.csv`; no test scores are available. The pool contains distinct static nonlinear map families sharing the data-supported periodic planar kinematics, rather than coefficient perturbations of one model.

sealed.note: the test error of the recommended candidate (practical selection); sealed

ranking.label: oracle-based selection on test data
ranking.note: This ranking selects on the test data. It measures whether the pool contains an accurate model, not whether the agent can recognize that model without test data. A rank is not evidence of physical admissibility: each entry carries its unresolved requirements and any violation allowed by the user.
ranking.tie_rule: |S_a - S_b| <= 1e-12 * max(S_a, S_b) for consecutive candidates; tied candidates share a rank

settings.discontinuities: expressions with jumps (Piecewise, sign) are evaluated pointwise at the sample instants and Runge-Kutta stages; no event detection or step refinement is applied at a jump
